facts.text: Director Gary Graver made this film for just $55,000. He put up $30,000 of his own money and raised the other $25,000 from investors and a distributor.
Peter Jason (Malcolm) has appeared in 12 Walter Hill films and is a John Carpenter regular, including They Live (1988) and Prince of Darkness (1987).
The two asylum attendants wrestling Malcolm into a straitjacket are played by football pros Dan Pastorini and Tim Rossovich, cast through friendships of actor Peter Jason, per Jason.
Graver shot the whole film at night, 6 PM to midnight, in about three weeks. By day he handled lab work, catering and editing for it.
The song 'Help Is on the Way' heard here is by the band Horizon, who later scored the 1983 film Suzie Superstar. Tom Barger wrote it.
Steve Railsback, the voice on the phone as Linda's boyfriend Brett, reunited with Carrie Snodgress nearly 20 years later, playing her son in a film about killer Ed Gein.
Carrie Snodgress (Joan) was Oscar-nominated for Diary of a Mad Housewife (1970). She reportedly lost the lead in Rocky (1976) over a salary dispute.
Most of the film was shot in the real home of Carrie Snodgress, who plays Joan. One night her ex Neil Young reportedly dropped by, unaware a movie was being shot.
The asylum's front facade is Culver Studios in Culver City, former home of RKO Radio Pictures, Thomas Ince Studios and Desilu.
David Carradine, as Richard, was the TV star of Kung Fu. Quentin Tarantino first offered Bill in Kill Bill to Warren Beatty, who suggested Carradine.
Peter Jason (Malcolm) says director Gary Graver pitched it as a kids' horror movie: 'Gary said Trick or Treats was going to be a kids' horror movie, so I said OK, fine.'
Prankster Christopher is played by Chris Graver, the director's own son. Richard Scheib of Moria said Chris plays obnoxiousness to perfection.
Orson Welles is credited as 'Magical Consultant'. Graver was Welles' last cinematographer, shooting The Other Side of the Wind, which finally came out in 2018.
Gary Graver volunteered to shoot Orson Welles' unfinished The Other Side of the Wind. That left him taking other jobs to pay the bills, which led to low-budget oddities like this one.
Gary Graver was a combat photographer in Vietnam before shooting B-movies for Roger Corman and others.
Historian Joseph McBride says Orson Welles did some last-minute script doctoring on this film. He also helped young Chris Graver with the magic.
Graver spent years directing hardcore porn as 'Robert McCallum'. Wikipedia says he worked on 135 adult features.
Richard Scheib of Moria notes the plot echoes Halloween (1978) and When a Stranger Calls (1979): a maniac escapes an asylum, heads home on Halloween and taunts a babysitter by phone.
Posters and covers for Dracula vs. Frankenstein, I Was a Teenage Werewolf, Maniac and The Howling show up as set dressing.
One record sleeve Christopher flips through is The Howling (1981), which starred John Carradine, father of David Carradine, who plays Christopher's stepfather.
Bands About Movies singled out the doorbell interludes as a highlight. Linda keeps answering the door to trick-or-treaters, hoping something big will happen.
The wino stripped here is Paul Bartel, who directed David Carradine in Death Race 2000 (1975) and later made Eating Raoul (1982).
The film editors griping about horror movies are Graver's friends. His wife Jillian is among them, in a cameo as an editor.
Director Gary Graver was blunt about his motive. He told Penny Blood magazine, 'I made Trick or Treats to make money.'
Catherine Coulson, the future Log Lady of Twin Peaks, has a cameo in this low-budget Halloween oddity.
Richard Scheib of Moria gave it two stars. He grumbled that nearly 70 minutes go to babysitting pranks before the real threat arrives.
Kansas City Star critic Robert C. Trussell wrote that one look at the script should have tipped off the producers that the film 'could never have been anything but a bomb.'
facts.byline: Robert C. Trussell — Kansas City Star

facts.text: Graver saw it as a comedy that suffered from being sold as a horror film. He said the distributor, also his partner, never paid him.
Richard Scheib of Moria says Linda's boyfriend Brett is played by Steve Railsback, who was married in real life to Jacqueline Giroux, the actress playing Linda.
Opening in Cincinnati on October 1, 1982, it was savaged by newspapers. Peter Jason recalled a first-week gross of about $75,000.
Film historian Joseph McBride, a friend of director Gary Graver, said of Graver's script: 'And Gary was not a good screenwriter.'
The tagline promised 'Halloween's over. Now it's the kids' turn to get even!'
Besides the 'kids' turn to get even' line, the film was also sold with the tagline '...when Halloween night stopped being fun!'
Graver sued Orson Welles' daughter Beatrice Welles in a dispute over an Oscar for Citizen Kane. He claimed Welles gave it to him. She won in 1993.
Groovy Doom's Bill Van Ryn considers this a remake of the 1971 thriller Fright, per Bands About Movies. It chased the success of Halloween.
AllMovie panned it, saying the plot holes in Graver's story are never plugged with cheap spectacle that might have given the film a reason to exist.
In 2004 Graver made a director's cut, trimming about ten minutes from the 90-minute film. He later owned the negative outright.
